title: tier — who stands behind a statement
description:
The epistemic tier of one entry. The enum and its definitions are weft's `ai.mythrl.tier` rider (weft/schemas/ai.mythrl.tier.json, `properties.tier`) VERBATIM, so a shed entry mirrored into a room is readable by weft's own rule; weft wraps this value in its envelope `{v, tier, by, from}` and shed carries it flat as `tier` because a shed entry already names its source (`evidence`, `origin_sid8`). Keep the enum equal to weft's — test_shed.py compares the two files when weft is checked out beside shed.

The line between these is ACCOUNTABILITY STRUCTURE, not species.

authored = an identified party — a person OR an AI peer — stands behind this as their own statement (a person's message, a hand-written pin, a peer's signed refusal).

derived = machine-computed from a determinate source and reproducible by re-running the computation; nobody's opinion (a sensor reading, commit metadata, a chain verification).

interpreted = stateless synthesis no one can be held to (a bot's summary, an enrichment, a synthesized observation).

Why authored is not 'a human wrote it': project_interpretation_tier constitutes the interpreted tier from two properties — no continuous identity, and no accountability surface. An AI peer holding an identity key has BOTH, so its signed statements fail the test for interpreted. Reading authored as human-only would mean a peer can never author anything, only emit output — encoding into the trust chrome the exact capability asymmetry the substrate exists to refuse.

Grounded-ness is NOT a tier. Whether an interpreted entry is a verbatim span or a paraphrase is whether `evidence` is present and survives the substring test (basis, not tier); the retired sub-tiers `extracted` / `synthesized` are unreadable, not a fourth tier. An unknown value is unreadable: weft's reader treats it as unstated, shed's finalize rejects it. There is deliberately NO 'unstated' value — absence is the unstated state and a reader MUST NOT fall through to `authored`; shed's gate goes one step further and refuses a tier-less entry outright, because a record that cannot say who stands behind a line should not carry it.
